items.stem:
Read the passage below, based on the story 'The Wit that Won Hearts', and answer.

"One morning, while the court was discussing the coming harvest, Tenali Rama stepped forward with a small cloth bag. 'Your Majesty,' he said with a bow, 'these are paddy seeds of a rare kind. They give a golden crop, but only if they are sown by a person who has never yawned.' The courtiers glanced at one another, and a few hid a smile."

Why did some courtiers hide a smile?
items.answer: They knew that everyone yawns, so the condition sounded impossible and suspected a trick.
items.markingKey: They knew that everyone yawns, so the condition sounded impossible and suspected a trick. (1–2 marks for a complete answer.)

items.stem: Do you think Tenali Rama took a risk by speaking to an angry king? Give reasons. Answer in about 40 words.
items.answer: Yes – an angry king could have punished him; but he chose a light, indirect way that made the king laugh instead of feel insulted.
items.markingKey: Accept any well-reasoned answer. Value points: Yes – an angry king could have punished him; but he chose a light, indirect way that made the king laugh instead of feel insulted. (2 marks: content and expression.)

items.stem:
Read the passage below, based on the story 'The Wit that Won Hearts', and answer.

"When two friends fall out over a small matter, pride often keeps them apart far longer than the quarrel itself. A gentle joke, a kind word or a shared memory can open the door again. Humour works because it lets both sides step back and see how small the problem really is."

Answer the following:
(i) Name two things that can "open the door again".
(ii) Why does humour work in such situations?
(iii) "Open the door again" here means …  (a) invite guests  (b) make it possible to become friends again  (c) leave the house  (d) start a new quarrel
(iv) How does this passage connect with the story of Tenali Rama?
items.answer: (i) A gentle joke, a kind word or a shared memory (any two). (ii) It helps both sides step back and see how small the problem is. (iii) (b) make it possible to become friends again (iv) Like the passage says, Tenali used humour to make the king see how small the matter was and end the quarrel.
items.markingKey: (i) A gentle joke, a kind word or a shared memory (any two). (ii) It helps both sides step back and see how small the problem is. (iii) (b) make it possible to become friends again (iv) Like the passage says, Tenali used humour to make the king see how small the matter was and end the quarrel. (1 mark each, 4 marks.)
